rationale: Load-bearing TokenKey-only frontend surfaces that anchor admin-UI behavior diverging from upstream defaults — sidebar geometry (TK uses a narrower w-44 rail vs upstream w-64), the fluid table mode used on /admin/accounts (no horizontal scroll, cells wrap), per-page sticky-edge-hints opt-out, and the control-plane login policy that does not depend on Turnstile. These are the kinds of small TK changes that get silently reverted by upstream merges precisely because they're small and local; the registry upgrades the rule from `agent must remember` to `merge will fail`. Source-of-truth read by both `scripts/preflight.sh` (frontend TK sentinel registry section, always) and `.github/workflows/upstream-merge-pr-shape.yml` (frontend TK sentinels check, on `merge/upstream-*` PRs). Adding a new TK-only frontend surface that must survive upstream merges MUST add a sentinel here in the same commit. Sibling registries: `newapi-sentinels.json` (fifth-platform integration), `brand-sentinels.json` (outward TK brand surfaces). This file now also guards upstream payment-surface carry-ins that touch shared admin/i18n/style hotspots during upstream merges; updating those hotspots in merge PRs requires explicit sentinel-registry rationale refresh or a `sentinel-registry-reviewed` / `upstream-merge` commit marker to keep the gate mechanical.

Quickstart and Studio derive their catalogs from this registry so Claude/Codex/Gemini/OpenCode and the newer Qwen/Cherry/Dify/Cline/Roo/LobeHub/Chatbox entries cannot drift into separate hand-maintained lists. AppSidebar.vue / AppLayout.vue import the sidebar constants so upstream-shaped layout files stay close to upstream; AdminShellView imports TK_ADMIN_UI_ZOOM for the ops default 80% scale. If either constant disappears, the import sites fail to compile (loud). The sentinel adds a second layer in case an upstream merge replaces the entire constants file.

The Media Studio (/studio) user-nav entry. Without this anchor an upstream merge to the nav builder could silently drop the Studio link, hiding the image/video generation surface from users while everything still compiles.

The /pricing media rendering branches (per-image / per-second) and shared catalog-modality owner wiring. TablePageLayout's `fluid` prop and matching modifier-scoped CSS rules. The fluid wrapper rule must keep `overflow-x-auto` (not `overflow-x-hidden`) so a narrow viewport falls back to a scrollbar instead of clipping rightmost columns. Sibling guard to the DataTable.vue fluid-overflow sentinel above — both paths must move in lockstep.

Shared usage-window quota summary de-duplication owner. Anchors keep upstream merges from silently dropping the generic usage badges on OAuth-only accounts or restoring duplicate quota chips.

Anchors keep upstream merges from silently dropping the generic usage badges on OAuth-only accounts or restoring duplicate Codex window chips.

The TK callsite for fluid+stickyEdgeHints opt-outs (first two literals), the wrap-first column-class policy comment (third literal), and the per-column max-width discipline (fourth + fifth literals). `wrap` as a function (not a plain string constant) means every column carries an explicit cap — an upstream merge that flattens it back to a bare string would silently drop the caps and the table overflows again at 100% browser zoom. The fifth literal anchors the usage column at 15rem (the widest cap), chosen because it is uniquely wide and unlikely to clash with any upstream string. Without the max-width caps, `min-w-0 align-top` alone is insufficient: browser table-auto still sizes columns to their natural max-content width when there is no explicit upper bound. The sixth literal anchors current_rpm inside shouldReplaceAutoRefreshRow's auto-refresh field whitelist: current_rpm is a Redis-backed realtime gauge that never bumps updated_at, so an upstream merge that drops it from the whitelist would silently regress the 6s auto-refresh back to RPM-stale (only manual refresh would update the RPM badge). The seventh literal anchors the admin notes (备注) display under the account name in the #cell-name template: operators edit notes in EditAccountModal but the only other notes render is a default-hidden column, so dropping this line would silently hide multi-line notes again — it is rendered with whitespace-pre-wrap so newlines edited by the operator survive verbatim. The EdgeAccountPanelTk/useTkAccountsEdgePanels anchors pin the /admin/accounts inline edge panels, and the refreshEdges({force:true}) anchors pin the manual refresh/retry path that bypasses the edge aggregate SWR cache so prod stubs and edge account runtime gauges sync on operator clicks.

Admin account-table default visible columns are TK operator workflow, not upstream defaults: platform/type, capacity, status, schedulable, groups, usage, and priority should be visible on a fresh profile, while scheduler_score stays hidden by default because showing it opts into heavy backend scoring. Legacy auto-saved defaults from version 1 or the scheduler-score migration version migrate once. The exact DEFAULT_HIDDEN_COLUMNS block pins the combined default so an upstream merge cannot silently hide priority or show scheduler_score again; the version-key and migration anchors keep old localStorage snapshots from resetting operators back to stale column sets after refresh.

Group-level messages compaction threshold wiring is a TK-only admin surface shipped with #142 follow-up. It is easy for upstream merges on large upstream-shaped GroupsView.vue to keep compile green while dropping either threshold normalization, payload field wiring, or the validation guard. These three literals pin all three layers.

Create-account modal must persist account-level compaction policy in extra fields. This path is a large upstream hotspot and prone to silent overwrite during merges; sentinel keeps toggle state, threshold state, and payload key wiring together.

Edit-account modal must load and update account-level compaction policy from extra. Compile still passes if only one half (read/write) is dropped; these literals pin the load/edit/persist chain for upstream-merge safety.

TK preserves the authenticated session across browser offline/network-change failures and turns Axios no-response failures into an explicit NETWORK_ERROR contract. This companion keeps the upstream-shaped client.ts to thin injection points; if an upstream merge removes this file or the contract literals, offline users can be logged out or background refresh can resume console/request storms.

The upstream-shaped Axios client must keep the TK injection points for network-error normalization, refresh-token network failure propagation, and protected-endpoint refresh without requiring a localStorage refresh token. The latter is required for HttpOnly cookie-only sessions; losing it clears an otherwise renewable session on the first 401.

The shared refresh coordinator must support both rotating localStorage tokens and HttpOnly cookie-only sessions. A nullable snapshot selects an empty JSON body for cookie fallback, withCredentials sends the cookie, and local-token race detection runs only when a local token actually existed.

must_contain: 无 localStorage refresh_token 时使用 cookie 刷新并重试原请求
refresh_token 请求遇到网络错误时保留 localStorage
cookie-only refresh 遇到网络错误时保留 localStorage
sentinels.rationale: Focused interceptor regressions prove cookie-only 401 recovery and preserve auth state on transient refresh network failures for both localStorage and HttpOnly cookie-only sessions. Both regressions are user-visible logout failures that can survive typecheck and build.

Auth background refresh must short-circuit while offline, refresh once when the browser comes back online, and keep a single active online listener across store re-initialization. These anchors guard the user-session preservation fix against upstream store rewrites that still compile but reintroduce refresh storms or listener leaks.

Subscription polling must return cached data while offline and suppress expected network-error logging. Otherwise a browser network transition causes repeated /subscriptions/active failures and noisy console output without changing UI state.

Global typography scale is a TK-only density choice: TokenKey intentionally maps Tailwind text-base to 15px and keeps heading steps slightly smaller than upstream defaults. This file is a tiny upstream merge hotspot because losing the fontSize extension compiles cleanly but silently restores larger UI text across admin and user pages.

The compact Tailwind scale must apply to default body copy, not only explicit text-* utilities. Without body text-base, unclassed prose and third-party/default text remain at browser 16px while classed UI shrinks, producing inconsistent density after upstream merges that still compile. This file now also anchors the Airwallex CTA visual contract (dark-mode high-contrast variant) used by the new payment flow; missing these literals compiles but silently regresses operator/user affordance.

Normal control-plane login is intentionally not gated on Cloudflare Turnstile; PR #119 kept Turnstile on registration, verification-code, and password-recovery flows while relying on login rate limiting for this path. Upstream-shaped LoginView.vue repeatedly brings back the widget/token wiring during merges and compiles cleanly, so this negative sentinel fails preflight/merge-shape if login once again renders, waits for, or submits a Turnstile token.

OAuth and passkey action captcha stays behind a thin auth companion while ordinary email/password login remains captcha-free. These anchors pin the companion injection and both protected action call sites so a future upstream merge cannot restore captcha to password login or silently drop Tencent/Aliyun protection from the dedicated OAuth/passkey endpoints.

The auth action companion intentionally excludes Cloudflare Turnstile and maps only Tencent/Aliyun action results to their backend compatibility fields. Keeping provider details here preserves upstream captcha capabilities without expanding the normal TokenKey login gate or thickening LoginView.vue.
EmailNotificationConfig must carry the Feishu write-only config flags. Without this type shape, frontend edits to email/report settings can silently omit Feishu fields or regress masking semantics.

Tab navigation keyboard accessibility (ARIA + arrow/home/end handlers), the fallback_model_anthropic default, and the upstream payment/scheduler form defaults plus save serialization stay in the root orchestrator. These can be silently reverted by template/script overwrites while keeping builds green.

Gateway forwarding settings extracted from SettingsView.vue. The two component anchors pin the upstream account-usage and experimental-scheduler settings injection points without growing the upstream-hot GatewayPanel state machine.

Focused regression coverage for the upstream settings carry-ins. Anchoring the navigation helper and all four control surfaces prevents a future merge from deleting the tests alongside the components and leaving only existence sentinels.

The Airwallex provider/method labels are also load-bearing for operator payment configuration and user recharge selection; upstream locale merges can drop them silently while code still compiles.

The pricing catalog i18n keys (tabMy='Group Catalog', exploreBanner) anchor the per-group pricing catalog feature so an upstream locale merge cannot silently strip them and degrade the segmented control + upgrade-banner UI to raw keys.

The default value for tk_anthropic_request_normalize_enabled stays in the root SettingsView form reactive. Must remain true by default so the normalize feature is on unless explicitly disabled.

Chinese i18n keys for the Anthropic request normalize admin toggle. Locked in lockstep with the en.ts counterpart so neither language can silently regress to raw key strings.

EditAccountModal.vue and CreateAccountModal.vue render `t('admin.accounts.poolMode*')` in the type=apikey branch for every platform; internal Anthropic edge stubs mark pool mode as system-managed because the backend reconciler owns those fields. The toggle still controls in-place same-account retry semantics (isPoolModeRetryableStatus + GetPoolModeRetryCount, default 1 retry on 401/403/429/502/503/504), which is meaningful for upstream pool routing. English counterpart of the pool-mode i18n lockstep above. Locked in lockstep with zh.ts so neither language can silently regress to raw key strings during an upstream merge of i18n files.

Chinese RPM capacity badge sticky-buffer suffix. Moves in lockstep with the en.ts counterpart above so neither language silently regresses to a raw key during an i18n upstream merge.

TK-only tier dropdown options (l1..l5) for the admin 'Set Tier' action. Display labels only — the backend embedded baseline owns the numeric tier values. Guards the constant against silent upstream-merge deletion that would break the tier modal import.

TK-only composable owning the per-account 'Set Tier' flow: opens/closes the modal, calls adminAPI.accounts.applyAccountTier, surfaces success/error toasts. TK-only modal for the admin 'Set Tier' action. Thin template that renders the tier options and the local-deployment-only scope warning (applying a tier writes ONLY this deployment's DB; fleet fan-out still needs the ops/anthropic pipeline). Guards against silent upstream-merge deletion.

TK-only i18n DEFINITIONS for the Tier Templates modal. TK-only edge admin-session handoff landing. Consumes the access JWT + refresh_token from the URL FRAGMENT (tk_session / refresh_token), persists refresh + expires (persistOAuthTokenContext) so the session self-renews, establishes the session on THIS (edge) origin via authStore.setToken, then redirects to the edge's own /admin/accounts. THREE load-bearing security properties: (1) history.replaceState scrubs the token AND refresh_token from the address bar / history immediately on load so a leaked URL can't be replayed from the bar; (2) safeNext rejects protocol-relative / external redirect targets (open-redirect guard) — only same-origin absolute paths are followed; (3) the tokens are read from the fragment (never a query param) so they are never sent to the server / logged. Silent deletion or weakening of any of these is a token-leak / open-redirect regression. Pairs with edge_tk_admin_session_handler.go (mint) + buildEdgeHandoffURL (prod).
